subject: Reserved commit terms and staggered start — Boreal Tech capacity planning
messages:
From: Alex Huang <alex.huang@borealtech.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@borealtech.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry: reserved commit terms and start windows

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this — we are re-evaluating our inference footprint and want to understand Redwood's Dedicated reserved commit options. High-level: our production workload needs sustained throughput (roughly 2k tokens/sec across peak front-ends, ~550M tokens/day) with predictable latency. We anticipate an initial ramp but need a firm path to production within the next 60–90 days.

Questions we need answered for procurement:
- Pricing for 12 / 24 / 36-month reserved commits (we prefer committed GPU-pool sizing rather than per-token for budgeting).
- Your recommended GPU pool equivalent (A100 or similar) to meet the throughput and how you measure that (p99 latency, tokens/sec).
- Options for a staggered start (phased ramp over 3 months) vs. single start date — and how billing/credits work if we delay the start.
- Throughput guarantees and SLA credits if you cannot meet the committed throughput during steady-state.
- Any discounts or credit structures you offer for upstream commit flexibility (e.g., if we commit to 24 months but need first 2 months ramped).

I've attached our workload forecast and an initial traffic profile (boreal_requirements_v1.xlsx). Procurement will need ballpark numbers by EOM to include in our vendor evaluation. Would appreciate a short pricing matrix + recommended commit level and a 30–45 minute sync next week.

Appreciate it —
Alex Huang
VP Engineering, Boreal Tech
alex.huang@borealtech.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@borealtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry: reserved commit terms and start windows

Alex —

Thanks for the clear brief and the forecast attachment. Short answer upfront: we can support a phased/staggered start and we offer laddered discounting for longer terms; the right commit baseline depends on how much burst vs sustained throughput you want reserved.

Ballpark options (for discussion):
- 12-month: 6 reserved GPU equivalents (sustained baseline) — base price $XXX,XXX/mo — typical discount compared to on-demand: ~18%.
- 24-month: 8 reserved GPU equivalents — base price $YYY,YYY/mo — ~25% discount.
- 36-month: 8–10 reserved GPUs with deeper quantization/placement optimizations — ~30% discount and optional reserved burst capacity.

Notes on ramping and credits:
- Staggered start: we can hold a commit with a 90-day start window; billing commences either on the agreed start date or when actual capacity is allocated (your choice).
- Delayed-start credit: if allocation slips >45 days beyond the agreed start we typically issue a pro-rata credit for the delayed period or shift invoicing to match allocation.
- Throughput SLOs: we provide throughput guarantees measured at 95/99 percentiles — for dedicated pools we set a throughput SLO for your routes and provide credits (service credits or additional short-term burst capacity) if we miss targets.

We also attach a short pricing matrix and a technical runbook (redwood_pricing_matrix_v3.pdf). Ben is looped in to validate the GPU sizing against your profiler. Can you share target p99 latencies and any peak concurrency patterns? I'll propose a couple of concrete commit packages and a DocuSign-ready term sheet after that.

Available slots for a 30-min sync: Mon/Thu mornings PT.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

From: Alex Huang <alex.huang@borealtech.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@borealtech.com>, Procurement <procurement@borealtech.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry: reserved commit terms and start windows

Grace —

Thanks for the quick ballpark. A few clarifications from Procurement:
- If we commit to 24 months and elect a staggered start (first 3 months at 40% of baseline, then ramp to 100%), how does the monthly invoice look? Do we pay full reserved fee from day 1 or do you invoice ramped amounts?
- For the delayed-start credit: can you make it contractually explicit (for procurement) that if Redwood misses allocation by >60 days we get an invoice credit equal to the monthly reserved fee for the missed month (not just pro-rata service credit)? Procurement needs a clean remedy.
- SLA: we need a measurable throughput SLO (tokens/sec at 99th percentile) and an escalation path (on-call contact, root-cause timeline, and credit up to X% of monthly fee).

We can provide p99 targets — our current constraint is 200–250ms p95 on short prompt flows.

Marta (copied) will join the vendor review; our decision window is end-of-month. Can you provide a redline-friendly term sheet and a sample DocuSign link to expedite?

— Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@borealtech.com>, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry: reserved commit terms and start windows

Alex / Grace —

On Mon, Apr 13, 2026 at 08:45 AM Alex Huang <alex.huang@borealtech.com> wrote:
> If we commit to 24 months and elect a staggered start (first 3 months at 40% of baseline, then ramp to 100%), how does the monthly invoice look?

Short technical note: the billing model we propose for staggered starts is flexible — we can bill the committed discount against an "on-book" capacity reservation and then invoice actual usage against that reservation. Practically: for a 24-month commit with a 3-month ramp at 40%, you'd see either 1) a phased invoice (40% of the reserved monthly fee for months 1–3, then 100%), or 2) full reservation charged up-front with a monthly credit applied until ramp completes. Option 1 is the more procurement-friendly approach.

On the SLA and throughput measurement: we baseline the pool with an internal perf run (we'll run your profiler) and set the throughput SLO in tokens/sec measured at 99th across a 30-day window. If SLO misses exceed the threshold we can offer service credits up to a pre-agreed cap (typically 10–25% of the monthly reserved fee depending on severity) and immediate allocation of temporary burst capacity while we remediate.

I'll attach the performance_runbook.pdf with how we measure tokens/sec and latency baselining. Happy to hop on a call to walk through measurement and reporting.

— Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@borealtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@borealtech.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Final proposal: laddered credit structure + staggered start (proposal attached)

Alex / Marta —

Thanks for the details — below is a concise proposal that addresses Procurement's asks and maps to the technical baseline Ben described. I'll produce a redline-friendly term sheet and DocuSign packet once you confirm the package.

Proposal summary (recommended):
- Commitment: 24 months (BRL-2026-042)
- Reserved pool: 8 GPU equivalents (sized to meet ~2k tokens/sec steady-state with headroom for routing/burst).
- Ramp: 3-month staggered start (month 1 = 40% baseline, month 2 = 70%, month 3 = 100%). Billing option: phased invoice (you pay 40/70/100% of reserved fee during months 1–3) — chosen to align with Procurement preferences.
- Credit for delayed allocation: if Redwood cannot allocate the reserved pool within 45 days of the agreed start date, Redwood will issue a monthly invoice credit equal to the reserved monthly fee for each full month of delay. (If you'd like this extended to 60 days for internal sign-off, we can discuss wording — procurement asked for 60; we propose 45 as vendor compromise.)
- SLA / throughput SLO: 99th-percentile tokens/sec measured over a rolling 30-day window. Remedies: service credits up to 20% of monthly reserved fee for sustained SLO misses; immediate allocation of temporary burst capacity during remediation. We will include on-call escalation contacts and an RCA timeline in the term sheet.
- Discounting / price: laddered effective discounts versus on-demand; final pricing attached in redwood_pricing_matrix_v3.pdf. Example effective discount for 24-month, 8-GPU: 25% off standard hosted rates (line-item pricing in attachment).

Next steps:
1) Confirm you want the 24-month / 8-GPU package and the 45-day delayed-allocation credit as written.
2) We'll prepare a term sheet + DocuSign packet (target: ready within 48 hours of confirmation).
3) Ben will schedule a 45-min baseline perf run next week (we need your profiler keys).

If you need Procurement-friendly wording to swap 45 -> 60 days, we can add a short clause showing that as an option with a 1% additional fee or tiered credit language.

Proposed 30-min call to finalize: Fri Apr 16, 09:30–10:00 PT — does that work?

Attachments: redwood_pricing_matrix_v3.pdf (term pricing matrix), performance_runbook.pdf (measurement details). DocuSign preview link will be provided after confirmation.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
